The major flaw with reverse-osmosis screens is that they tend to trap a lot of the salt that they're designed to remove. This means that they get all clogged up with salt and filter less and less water over time. Setting someone up with a screen does not ensure a steady supply of drinkable water for a long time, it sets them up with a supply of fresh (But not neccessarily clean) water for a modest amount of time.

True breakthroughs in reverse osmosis will not just be from cheap filtering material, but cheap and effective ways to un-clog or easily replace and recycle existing screens.

Also, the process traps salts because the molecules are the right size to be strained or trapped by the mesh, there are a great deal of contaminants that would not be filtered out by this method.

On Metacritic Yooka Laylee is mostly averaging out to mixed reception. Some could see this as karma for their JonTron controversy, but from the looks of it, it seems like the game is mostly getting flak for being too hard in today's commoncore standard of games.

Either way, here is the link: http://www.metacritic.com/game/playstation-4/yooka-laylee
Yooka Laylee getting mostly mixed reviews.

Skimming the reviews, most seem to complain that the game is too "dated", ignoring that's exactly what people want out of the game: an authentic N64-era styled platformer. Everything is so controlled and tutorialized these days and I miss games where you have to explore and experiment to beat it. Yooka Laylee seems to be exactly that and I love what I've seen (waiting for a sale though).

Question: Dated or old-school? There's a difference between these two.

Let's take Doom 1 for an example. Fast-paced action is old-school but the original control scheme is dated.

I'm leaning towards old-school from what I've seen and don't trust a majority of reviewers to make the distinction. Neither the sites I do trust nor the streamers I watch have gotten their hands on it yet. That's the other big thing I'm waiting on.

From what I've seen, the collecting aspect and general design is about on par to Banjo/DK64. This means it comes down to how tightly the game and camera controls. That's something you can't really analyze until either you get your own hands on it, a reviewer you trust gets their hands on it, or you watch streams/let's plays of it.
So Wildcard has given the lowest review score.

Skimmed through the reviews as well. Most of what they are complaining about is pretty much what I want from the game. Whether it will be as enjoyable as I think remains to be seen, but so far I have no concerns.

It was only really Donkey Kong 64 that was hard because it made you backtrack every level with all five characters in order to collect everything.

I just played through Banjo Kazooie a few days ago, and it was honestly pretty chill, you can pretty much find everything through casual exploration.
